scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The origins of the Nutbush dance trace back to the 1970s disco era in Australia.
Although named after the track 'Nutbush City Limits' by Ike & Tina Turner, Tina Turner herself never performed the routine.

A 2024 study by the University of South Australia and Edith Cowan University suggested that the New South Wales Department of Education developed the dance as a teaching aid in the mid-1970s, potentially based on the Madison dance or an adapted version of the sequence associated with 'Alley Cat'.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The Nutbush is a secular social line dance performed at Australian school events, community gatherings, weddings, and music festivals.
It serves as an accessible participatory group activity where simple steps allow dancers of all ages and skill levels to join together.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: The people
narration: While Tina Turner wrote and recorded the namesake song 'Nutbush City Limits', she never performed the line dance.
The dance was institutionalized by physical education developers within the New South Wales Department of Education during the mid-1970s.

A widely recognized variation occurs during the final 4 beats, known as the 'criss-cross': dancers jump both feet outward on beat 1, jump to cross legs on beat 2, jump to uncross outward on beat 3, and clap on beat 4.
The Nutbush inherits structural elements from earlier 20th-century American line dances like the Madison and the Alley Cat.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1: Touch right foot to the side and return twice, then touch left foot to the side and return twice (8 beats)

Footwork from the sources: Side touches right and left (8 counts), back touches right and left (8 counts), knee raises (8 counts), cross kicks (4 counts), quarter turn and clap (4 counts).

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer
narration: Step 3: Raise right knee across body to left hip twice, then raise left knee across body to right hip twice (8 beats)
Step 4: Kick right leg across body once, then kick left leg across body once (4 beats)
Drill: Practice double right back touch and left back touch on beat

scenes.title: Put it together
narration: Step A, then Step B, without stopping. Slow first.
